To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the five main hormones, auxins, cytokinin, ethylene, GA3, and ABA, affect hairy roots of Artemisia annua in different ways.
6-benzilaminopurine (BA) and 2-isopenyladenine (2-IP) inhibit root growth, however 2-IP stimulates artemisinin production by 200% over the control.
1) the highest biomass production was achieved with ABA, 2) 2-isopentoxyadenine was the most effective cytokinin for stimulating artemisinin production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of phytoharmone on the growth of Artemisia annua L. hairy root cultures.
the effect of phyto-hormones on growth of Artemisia annua L. hairy roots.
the effect of phyto-hormones on hairy root growth, development and production of secondary metabolites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most important factors in increasing artemisinin production are the presence of a cytokinin, and the absence of auxins, gibberellin, and abscisate.
the effect of phytochemicals on hairy roots is complex and depends on many factors.
6-benzilaminopurine inhibits growth of A. annua hairy roots, while 2-isopentylenyladenine stimulates artemisinin production and 0.01mgl−1 GA3 stimulates growth and artemisin production in A. annua.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
2-isopenthyladenine is the best cytokinin to stimulate artemisinin production and that GA3 is the most effective in increasing total root length.

the best conditions for growth and artemisinic acid production in A. annua hairy roots are: 0.01 mg l−1 GA3 for root elongation, 0.02 mg l−1 2-isopentanyladenine for artemisinic yield, 0.01 ml−1 1.0 ml−1 ABA for biomass yield.
the most important factor in the production of artemisinin in A. annua hairy roots is the concentration of the phytohormone 2-isopenthyladenine (2-IP).
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single hormone can have multiple effects on a hairy root culture.
the effect of a hormone on growth and artenisin production is dependent on both the type of hormone and its concentration.
the effects of a hormone depend on the type and concentration of that hormone.
